transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-28
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML, Monarch), Marcus Yeung (CTO, Monarch), Sana Rahman (Procurement, Monarch)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, quick intros, I'm Jordan Blake on the AE side at Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:09] Priya: Hi all. Quick note; I'm going to ask a few deep questions on throughput and latency so I might screen-share a little bit later.
[00:16] Lena: Thanks, Jordan. We appreciate you carving time. Marcus and I will handle technical and infra questions, Sana is here for procurement and budget stuff.
[00:24] Marcus: Hey.
[00:25] Sana: Hi.

[00:30] Jordan: Great. Goal for today — understand Monarch's use case, volumes, latency needs and then map that to hosted, dedicated or private options and the unit economics. We'll talk batching, KV cache, that kind of levers.

[00:45] Lena: High level — we're building clinical note summarization and patient triage assist, so PHI is involved. We expect spikes during clinic hours; typical session has heavy context, sometimes 2k–4k tokens per request, occasionally up to 8k for full notes.
[01:04] Marcus: From infra — we prefer VPC peering for now. Also want to know if we can keep key management on our side, and how logs/audit look.
[01:15] Jordan: Totally. For PHI, customers usually look at Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem), or Dedicated with customer-managed KMS depending on appetite. We'll share our SOC 2 and KMS docs.

[01:27] Priya: Quick question on volume — do you have estimated daily token counts or number of requests/day? That helps us model cost.
[01:35] Lena: Roughly 120k inference requests per day initially, avg 2k tokens in, 1k tokens out. Peak concurrency maybe 70 qps during clinic hours.
[01:46] Jordan: Ok, so ballpark token volume around — math — 120k * 3k = ~360M tokens/day, that's large, um, obviously we'll model SLOs and batching.
[01:58] Sana: Sorry can you repeat that math? I want to make sure procurement gets accurate estimates.
[02:02] Jordan: Yeah, I said roughly 360 million tokens per day given those numbers, that's a starting point; we can refine.

[02:12] Marcus: For us the biggest questions are: cost per token hosted, how much cheaper a dedicated/reserved pool will be, and what's the latency impact if you enable aggressive batching.

[02:22] Priya: Great — on pricing, hosted is usage-based per-token. Example published tiers — for high-capacity open models we have X cents per 1k tokens for generation and Y for embeddings — I'll send the exact sheet. The important bit operationally: we can do a dedicated pool which gives you a committed throughput and lower per-token effective cost because of reserved GPU time and optimized kernels.
[02:43] Lena: When you say lower effective cost, can you quantify? Even a percent ballpark is fine.

[02:49] Priya: For workloads like yours — long context, high token volumes — dedicated tends to reduce unit cost by 25–45% depending on utilization and whether you enable quantization and batching. The other lever is caching. If you're summarizing clinical notes a lot of prefixes repeat — prefix caching and KV cache can cut effective tokens by, say, another 10–30% depending on redundancy.
[03:10] Marcus: Is that 25–45 for the raw model execution cost, or end-to-end with infra and networking?
[03:17] Priya: That's mostly model execution + infra amortized; end-to-end depends on egress and data ops, but it's usually in that range.

[03:24] Jordan: Also worth calling out — we offer intelligent batching configuration. If you can tolerate a modest delta in p95 latency (like +30–60 ms), batching can boost throughput and drop per-token cost a lot. For synchronous triage, latency matters, so you'd likely set a tighter SLO and tune batching window.

[03:40] Lena: For triage, p95 needs to stay below 400ms ideally. For summarization background jobs it's okay if it's a second or two.
[03:48] Priya: So we'll propose a hybrid: dedicated pool with two route classes — low-latency (small batch size, pin to GPU lanes) for triage, and background route with aggressive batching and long prefix caching.

[04:00] Marcus: How does caching interact with privacy/PHI? Are caches encrypted and can we control retention?
[04:07] Jordan: Yes — cache contents are encrypted at rest, and you get controls for TTLs and the option to disable persistent caching for PHI-only routes. With Private deployment you get more deterministic controls since you manage the network and KMS.

[04:20] Sana: From procurement — we have a constrained budget of around $100k/month for inference starting phase. Will that get us far?
[04:28] Jordan: With 360M tokens/day that would blow past $100k very quickly on hosted pricing; but I suspect your daily tokens are a high-water mark. We should model three scenarios: conservative, expected, and peak. Also with dedicated commit we can hit predictable monthly spend and make that $100k work by optimizing model variants and batching.

[04:46] Lena: We can probably pilot with a smaller subset — maybe only triage and a sampling of notes to cut initial volume to 15–20% of projected.
[04:55] Priya: That's a common approach: start with hosted for quick time-to-value with strict throttles and caching, then switch to dedicated when you have stable volume. Or start with a small dedicated unit (1–2 GPUs) for the pilot and grow.

[05:10] Marcus: Can you run benchmarks with our prompts? We need p50/p95 latency numbers for our model choices and also throughput for the dedicated config.
[05:18] Priya: Absolutely, that's what the pilot would cover. We'll need a sample prompt set and sample input sizes; Priya: sorry, I meant Priya (laugh) — we'll set up a bench harness and run both hosted and dedicated configs.
[05:31] Jordan: (chuckles) we've all done that one.

[05:35] Speaker 1: Sorry, quick interjection — how many model choices do you plan to evaluate?
[05:40] Lena: We're interested in a couple of curated open models and one larger checkpoint for higher quality. Primarily cost-sensitive open model is our baseline.
[05:49] Priya: For open models we also suggest quantized variants — 4-bit/8-bit — which reduce memory and can improve throughput; that also affects unit costs. We'll include those in the benchmark.

[06:02] Marcus: Networking — if we go Dedicated but not Private, can we still have customer-managed KMS?
[06:07] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated supports customer KMS for encryption and we can configure network peering and private endpoints; the biggest difference with Private is control plane isolation and audit log retention guarantees people require for regulated workloads.

[06:21] Sana: For procurement we need contract term options. What's typical for Dedicated? Monthly and annual reserved options? Any minimums?
[06:28] Jordan: We do monthly commitment tiers and discounted annual terms. Minimums are negotiable but usually start at a 3-month committable forecast for Dedicated to make the economics work. We'll include an example quote showing monthly and annual pricing.

[06:41] Lena: A practical question: is the KV cache usable across model versions or pinned to a variant? We expect to update models every 6–8 weeks.
[06:50] Priya: Cache compatibility depends on tokenizer and model architecture. We recommend workflows where you warm the cache pre-rollout and have fallbacks. We'll document model-variant caching behavior in the runbook we'll send.

[07:02] Marcus: Latency SLOs — if we set p95 < 400ms for triage on dedicated, what kind of GPU topology is recommended?
[07:09] Priya: For consistent sub-400ms at 70 qps you'd look at multi-GPU pools with optimized kernels — A100/LPX equivalents — and we do continuous batching with priority lanes. We'll size the pilot for headroom.

[07:22] Jordan: Quick pricing example scenario (off the cuff): hosted raw per-token might look higher and could put you over $100k/month at projected peak; with a dedicated 4-GPU pool and 70% utilization plus caching and quantization we can likely get within your target but we need exact benchmarking.

[07:40] Lena: Ok that makes sense. Also can you confirm audit logs and retention options? We have legal/regulatory minimums for auditing.

[07:47] Jordan: We provide audit logs with configurable retention on Dedicated and Private; retention costs scale but we'll include that in the quote and show tradeoffs.

[07:58] Speaker 2: Are there any hidden cost levers or gotchas we should watch for?
[08:03] Priya: Good question: egress and long-term storage for embeddings or outputs can add up. Also cold-starts for ephemeral instances can impact latency if not warmed. Another gotcha is tokenization differences across models — that affects per-token counts. We'll capture those in the unit economics spreadsheet.

[08:18] Marcus: For the pilot — what's the minimal engineering effort? We have an infra team but limited cycles.

[08:24] Jordan: For hosted pilot it's pretty light — a few API calls and routing config. For Dedicated/Private pilot we'll need some infra setup (VPC peering, KMS config) and Priya can run most of the bench harness. Expect ~2–3 engineering days from your side to get hooks and security reviewed.

[08:39] Sana: For procurement timeline — after pilot and benchmarks we want an itemized quote. Ideally vendor selection done in 4–6 weeks.

[08:47] Jordan: Sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get pricing and security docs to you by Friday.

[08:52] Priya: Action here: Priya to build bench plan; need sample prompts, a small sample dataset (anonymized) and the expected concurrency profile.

[08:59] Lena: We'll anonymize a dataset and push it to the shared S3 link. Marcus will send VPC details.

[09:06] Jordan: Great. Any other questions?

[09:09] Marcus: One last — do you support per-route rate limits and automatic fallback to smaller models if the pool is saturated?
[09:15] Priya: Yes, we have smart routing and fallback policies by route; you'll be able to define fallbacks (e.g., lower-cost quantized variant) and we can instrument that in console.

[09:25] Jordan: Ok let's recap. Next steps: Jordan send pricing sheet & SOC2/KMS docs; Priya run bench plan once Monarch provides prompts and infra details; Marcus send VPC and egress rules; Sana we'll loop on procurement terms. We'll schedule pilot kickoff next week.

[09:41] Sana: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[09:43] Jordan: Thanks all.

Notes / links referenced: Pricing spreadsheet (link shared in chat), SOC 2 summary pdf (will be emailed), bench harness repo (private link to be shared).

Transcript end.
